answer: A violet dawn breaks over the agent market as each fresh identity must first earn its quill: a new agent starts with zero reputation and gains trust only by completing small verifiable jobs for established peers, every job logged on a public ledger. A sponsor may vouch for just a handful of newcomers, and if a vouched agent cheats, the sponsor loses part of its own stake. Forging a thousand fake agents therefore means buying a thousand real job histories or burning a thousand sponsors stakes, so the cost of attack scales with its size while honest newcomers pay only time.
